page: Amazon Web Services m6id.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose instance engineered for workloads requiring direct hardware access without hypervisor virtualization. Powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors based on the x86_64 architecture, the platform supplies 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.5 GHz. Compute resources are balanced with 512 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a uniform 4 GB per vCPU allocation. The CPU subsystem features 54 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration through VAES and SHA-NI.

Storage and networking subsystems are configured for high-throughput demands. The server integrates 7,600 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Synthetic evaluations demonstrate top-tier execution in multi-core parallel workloads, PassMark CPU benchmarks, cryptographic tests, and ray tracing. Memory throughput is strong, exceeding 339 GB/sec in large uncached block reads. Application benchmarks register 111.37 million Redis SET operations per second and 73.53 GB/sec in static web throughput. Conversely, single-core processing metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench register in average tiers, establishing that performance gains depend heavily on multi-threaded parallel execution.

From an infrastructure perspective, the server offers high resource consolidation by pairing extensive dedicated compute with fast NVMe storage and 50 Gbps networking. The absence of a discrete GPU limits its application profile to CPU-bound tasks. This bare-metal platform is well suited for high-density container orchestration, production relational databases, high-throughput in-memory caching tiers, large-scale Clang compilation workloads, and I/O-intensive data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores clocked at 3.5 GHz, paired with 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The platform integrates 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, operating without discrete GPU acceleration. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, VAES, and native virtualization flags without hypervisor overhead. Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust encryption throughput, and high memory bandwidth, though single-core performance remains in the average tier. The aggregation of dedicated compute, high-throughput local storage, and 50 Gbps networking provides high resource density for enterprise architectures. Amazon Web Services m6id.metal serves high-capacity databases, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, distributed data processing, enterprise application hosting, and software compilation pipelines.
